title: Lunar Landing Site Navigator - site catalog
frame: MOON_ME (mean Earth / polar axis, DE421 realisation) - the LOLA/LROC/IAU Gazetteer frame
conventions: lat_deg: planetocentric latitude, deg, [-90, 90]; lon_deg: EAST longitude, deg, [0, 360); height_m: metres above the 1737.4 km sphere or null (read from DEM); Site.origin is 'catalog' for every entry; extra.accuracy.kind tells landed point vs region centre.
pgda_sampling_note: extra.pgda_avg_illumination_at_point = value of the NASA GSFC PGDA / LOLA PDS average-solar-illumination map (18.6-yr hourly average, observer at the surface) at the catalog point: 'pixel_pct' = containing pixel, 'max3x3_pct' = max of the 3x3 neighbourhood; the 60 m/px product (AVGVISIB_85S_060M, a +-151.7 km polar-stereographic square) where it covers the point, else the 120 m/px AVGVISIB_75S_120M; sampled 2026-11-13. Independent second-method reference only.

sites.name: Artemis III region: Peak near Cabeus B
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate region map (Oct 2024; George et al., LPSC 2026, NTRS 20250011660), centre measured after georeferencing to Bertone et al. 2026 region centres
sites.note: APPROXIMATE centre of an extended candidate region measured on NASA's map; regional comparison only.

extra.frame: MOON_ME assumed: positions measured on NASA's 9-region map (LRO WAC mosaic) after georeferencing it to LOLA-frame region centres; frame of the map itself is LOLA-controlled

accuracy.description: Centre of the region box drawn on NASA's 2024 map, measured by georeferencing the map (estimated error <= 2 km). Box size ~21.3 x 21.9 km. NASA has not published numeric coordinates for this region; not a landing site.

extra.position_method: Centre and corners measured on the region map published with NASA's Oct 2024 update (image 1 of George et al., LPSC 2026, NTRS 20250011660; same map as the NASA news release). The map was georeferenced with a 4-parameter similarity transform fitted to the centres of the 5 regions that also appear in the 2022 list (Bertone et al. 2026, Zenodo 17954508): residuals 0.2-1.3 km; the 'South Pole' star maps 0.6 km from the pole; 1 px = 0.56 km. Plausibility: IAU crater Cabeus B (82.259 S, 305.415 E) lies ~65 km north of the box.

validation_facts.description: Sun elevation above the local horizon at the Apollo 11 LM touchdown
validation_facts.tolerance_rationale: 10.8 deg is the commonly quoted mission value (stated in the project brief); NASA documents give consistent but coarser numbers: Armstrong 'about 10 degrees Sun angle' ~30 min after landing (ALSJ, GET 103:12:44) and 'sun angle ranged from 14.5 to 16 deg' during the EVA (Apollo 11 Mission Report MSC-00171, sec. on EVA), i.e. ~6.5-9 h later at ~0.5 deg/h. JPL Horizons (airless apparent, sphere zenith) gives 10.70 deg. +-0.5 deg covers the quoting precision and local-slope effects.
validation_facts.source: Apollo 11 Mission Report MSC-00171 (NTRS 19710015566), EVA sun angle 14.5-16 deg; Apollo Lunar Surface Journal post-landing transcript (Armstrong: 'about 10 degrees Sun angle'); landing time NSSDCA 1969-059C

validation_facts.description: Sun elevation during the Apollo 11 EVA (approx. 1969-07-21T02:39 to 05:11 UTC)
validation_facts.tolerance_rationale: Mission report rounds to 0.5 deg and the EVA start/end times are approximate (+-several min).
validation_facts.source: Apollo 11 Mission Report MSC-00171 (NTRS 19710015566): 'During the extravehicular activity, the sun angle ranged from 14.5 to 16 deg'

validation_facts.description: At Chang'e-4 and Chang'e-6 the Earth centre never rises above the geometric horizon: both sites are >130 deg from the mean sub-Earth point, while libration (<~8 deg), topocentric parallax (~1 deg) and Earth's angular radius (~1 deg) total < 11 deg beyond 90 deg.
validation_facts.source: Geometry; far-side status per LROC/CNSA landing reports

validation_facts.description: Permanently shadowed floor points must receive no direct sunlight over multi-year simulations.
validation_facts.source: PGDA LPSR_85S_060M_201608 / AVGVISIB_85S_060M_201608 (Mazarico et al. 2011 method)
